mixer_geometry.response: Root is stabilizing mixer geometry when failure/success notices appear or disappear and when send routes are added. Controls should remain at the same positions through those changes. No completed-fix or new participant result is claimed in this draft.
mixer_geometry.basis: Four independent reports identify missed gestures after observable vertical movement.
mixer_geometry.validation_needed: App E2Es for unchanged control rectangles across error/success notices and send creation, including small viewports; fresh round8 mixer tasks.

audio_failure.response: The CPAL/ALSA output failure is under separate investigation. Preserve the exact observed failures and recovery outcomes; do not claim the backend cause or sustained-playback fix until reproduced and validated.
audio_failure.basis: Every participant reported a stream failure under the virtual ALSA/Pulse laboratory setup. Several captures include snd_pcm_avail_delay EIO.
audio_failure.validation_needed: Backend evidence, controlled reproduction and appropriate unit/native integration coverage; distinguish physical-device behavior from the virtual backend.

audio_recovery.response: Retry and selecting the named output provided visible transport/meter recovery for some participants. Preserve these controls and success observations, while linking them to the unresolved underlying failure; meters and playhead movement do not establish heard audio or long-term reliability.
audio_recovery.validation_needed: Any recovery implementation change must retain current position/error ownership and avoid restarting a healthy stream.

precise_trim.response: All five final WAVs independently verified as exactly30.000 seconds. Four reports needed a second snapped edge correction; this remains friction, not a newly proven trim defect. Preserve snap/source/Undo semantics and the existing Properties123 duration keypad, which participant3 used successfully for an exact endpoint. Recommend the exact-value route when a zoomed-out edge drag lacks sufficient precision.
precise_trim.validation_needed: Retain existing precise-trim and duration-entry regressions; no claim that one-drag precision is universally resolved.

loop_scope.response: Participant4 left a30.134-second playback loop while the arrangement and exported WAV were30.000 seconds. The loop and arrangement are separate editable ranges; trimming a clip should not silently rewrite a deliberately set playback loop. Record the distinction and preserve visible range readouts.
loop_scope.validation_needed: Retain playback-loop scope and arrangement-export tests; do not report the unchanged loop as a wrong export duration.

duplicate_tool.response: The toolbar selects a persistent Duplicate tool and already displays Click a clip to duplicate; the context-menu Duplicate command performs an immediate copy. Participant2 independently used both successfully. Keep those distinct, consistent behaviors and existing guidance. Repeated one-clip copying can take many clicks; this round does not establish a defect or justify changing tool selection into an immediate action.
duplicate_tool.validation_needed: Retain visible tool-gesture and immediate context-menu regressions. Any future bulk-repeat discovery work needs separate evidence; no new duplicate fix claimed.

native_dialog.response: Keep the transient GTK paint delay, upper-left placement and visual mismatch as observed limitations. Native dialogs ran without a window manager; these captures do not isolate an app defect or establish desktop behavior. Do not claim this fixed by mixer changes or replace native file pickers solely from this simulation.
native_dialog.validation_needed: Independent native-desktop reproduction if pursuing a picker change; save/export completion remains verified.

name_key_confusion.response: Participant3 mistook apostrophe for lowercase l, then used Clear and successfully applied little orbit. Preserve editable drafts, Clear and explicit Apply. Record glyph discrimination as a usability observation, without attributing the typo to a proven keyboard defect or claiming the unrelated numeric keypad work fixes it.
name_key_confusion.validation_needed: Existing mouse naming/Apply tests remain relevant; any letter-glyph redesign needs visual validation.

pan_diagonal.response: Participant4 needed a horizontal correction after diagonal pan dragging; displayed values provided recovery. Record the diagonal-gesture expectation mismatch. The independent review-driven final-release fix is not evidence that this participant’s diagonal direction issue was caused or solved by release handling.
pan_diagonal.validation_needed: Retain horizontal/vertical/release gesture tests; do not attribute an untraced native gesture to a specific implementation bug.

sparse_mixer_space.response: Participant3 found unused room with three channels. Preserve readable channel widths and space for additional channels; adding filler panels would conflict with the focused workspace. This is an appearance preference, not an established missing feature.
sparse_mixer_space.validation_needed: Keep compact-window reachability and alignment review alongside the geometry correction.

export_wait.response: WAV export took visibly longer than editing/MIDI export and showed elapsed progress. Preserve asynchronous export and clear completion receipts; these software-rendered laboratory sessions are not throughput benchmarks, and no faster export or completion-time estimate is claimed.
export_wait.validation_needed: Retain asynchronous export/progress/receipt tests; evaluate throughput separately if measured.

untested_scope.response: Requested composition, mixer and export features were found. Effects, recording, automation, other plug-ins and physical hardware were not covered by these sessions; leave them explicitly untested rather than treating non-exploration as absence or claiming full compatibility.
untested_scope.validation_needed: Do not expand completeness claims beyond observed tasks and independent saved-output verification.

positive.response: Preserve this observed successful workflow. findings.observation: Double-clicking the visible MIDI drop area opened the instrument library; Assign instrument created a MIDI track showing Rill Lab Sine.

Generate notes previewed an arpeggio on the piano roll. I selected minor triad and 0.5x speed, then used Next range to create C minor, F minor, G minor, and C minor phrases; the arrangement title showed 0:30.000.
Clicking Duplicate repeatedly selected a tool without adding clips. The hint then said Click a clip to duplicate; clicking the clip added an adjacent copy.
Duplicated drums reached 34.286 seconds. Trimming the last right edge first produced 30.134 seconds; a small second drag aligned the duration to 30.000.
Dragging mixer faders changed displayed levels to -7.5 dB for drums and -7.1 dB for the MIDI instrument. Horizontal pan drags displayed L11 and R13.

The audio-error banner appeared and disappeared during playback retries, changing mixer control positions. My first attempts at Solo hit the old vertical position; a later screenshot showed the Solo button active.
Add bus created New bus. The instrument Add send button opened routing; + Send offered New bus. Selecting it showed a 0.25x Post send, and the mixer displayed a routing line to the bus.
Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. I used its on-screen keys to enter rain, applied the name, and saved rain.rill through the native picker. The unsaved indicator disappeared.
WAV export showed Arrangement 0:30; I unchecked effect tails and accepted rain.wav. Both WAV and MIDI exports displayed explicit Exported notices.
Initial Play and Retry playback attempts produced Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Error details named an ALSA snd_pcm_avail_delay I/O error and System default output.

I opened Audio setup from the error banner, selected Rill lab paced output instead of System default, and applied. A subsequent Play showed a moving playhead and active audio, MIDI, bus, and master meters.
After playback recovered, I again activated drum Mute and instrument Solo, observed highlighted buttons, restored both, stopped playback, and saved.

Double-clicking the visible blank lane opened the Device library. Assign instrument created a MIDI track showing Rill Lab Sine. Double-clicking its pattern opened the piano roll, where Pencil drags created C4, C4, G4, F4 notes.
Clip context-menu Duplicate appended a drum clip. The toolbar Duplicate tool then showed Click a clip to duplicate and appended additional audio and MIDI clips. Fit exposed the whole arrangement.

Dragging the final audio edge to the visible 30-second line initially produced 0:30.134. A second four-pixel drag changed the project duration to 0:30.000. MIDI duplication required repeated clicks on successive clips.
The first Play click left the playhead at the start and displayed Audio output stream failed or disconnected, with Retry playback and Audio setup controls.

Retry playback changed Play to Pause. The following Mixer screenshot showed transport 003.02.15, active audio and MIDI channel level bars, and active master meters; later transport values advanced. No audio was auditioned.

Mixer fader drags visibly changed drums from -6.0 to -7.5 dB and MIDI from -2.5 to -8.6 dB. Horizontal knob drags changed pan to L16 and R21. Mute and Solo buttons gained distinct active outlines, and both were returned to off.

Add bus immediately created New bus. The MIDI Add send button opened Routing; + Send offered New bus, and selecting it displayed a 0.25x Post send. The mixer then showed Send · New bus and a routing line to the bus.

Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Its on-screen keys and Clear allowed the name pulse to be entered entirely with mouse clicks. Save defaulted to pulse.rill in session-2; accepting the picker returned to the app with the saved title.
Native save/export pickers appeared in the upper-left corner over the app; the WAV picker was briefly black before its contents appeared in a later screenshot. This did not block completion.

WAV export displayed Arrangement · 0:30, 48 kHz, Stereo, 32-bit float. I disabled effect tails, accepted pulse.wav, and saw Exported · pulse.wav. MIDI export defaulted to pulse.mid and showed Exported · pulse.mid after acceptance.

Playback advanced but stopped with Audio output stream failed or disconnected on two visible occasions. Error details reported ALSA snd_pcm_avail_delay I/O error (5), 48000 Hz and 1024 frames.

The error banner and the new send changed the vertical positions of the Mixer controls. Some attempted pan and solo gestures landed at the former positions and did not change the intended control; inspecting the new layout allowed correction.

Add bus created New bus. The instrument Add send button opened Routing; + Send offered New bus. Choosing it showed a 0.25x Post send, and the Mixer showed Bus 1 in plus a Post send to New bus routing arrow.

Play produced Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Retry playback briefly displayed Pause; the transport advanced from 001.01.00 to 003.01.30 before the same error returned. Subsequent control changes briefly showed Pause again. Sustained playback and audible balance were not established.

File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Mouse clicks on its on-screen keys entered night drive. Save opened a native dialog already in session-5, using night drive.rill; OK closed it and the title no longer showed the modified dot.

rating_reservations.reason: Visible double-click-for-MIDI guidance, the instrument assignment button, note generator, and labeled mixer controls let me complete the requested mouse workflow. Duplicate behaved as a tool instead of an immediate command, and exact trimming took a second drag.
The dark teal arranger, visible note previews, colored bus, and routing lines made the project feel coherent and polished. The native file picker looked visually separate.

Generating 56 notes and duplicating audio took few actions, and MIDI export returned quickly. Initial playback errors and retry attempts slowed the session; WAV export displayed a running elapsed counter before success. This rating is subjective and includes laboratory conditions.

Most main labels were clear. Duplicate required clicking a clip after choosing the tool. Reappearing audio-error banners moved the mixer controls vertically, causing missed solo clicks. System default output failed until I selected the named lab output.

I found audio and MIDI arrangement, a VST3 instrument, note generation, volume/pan/mute/solo, a bus and send, a mouse naming keyboard, project save, and both exports. I did not test effects, recording, automation, or other plug-ins.
Visible double-click guidance led directly to the instrument library; Pencil, Duplicate, Mixer, and export labels were usable without keyboard input. Exact trimming needed a small correction.
The dark interface, colored waveforms, clear notes, channel strips, and routing lines looked coherent and polished. Native save dialogs looked visually separate.

Most clicks and drags produced immediate visible changes; repeated MIDI clips were quick to create. Playback needed one retry and native dialogs sometimes appeared after an extra screenshot. WAV export showed elapsed progress and completed.
Low overall confusion because tools describe their actions. Initial playback failure and the very small trim adjustment were the main interruptions; a send required a routing panel and another menu.
rating_reservations.additional_response: A send required Routing and destination selection. All five discovered and completed it; explicit source/destination selection is retained to avoid ambiguous routing. No reduction in steps is claimed.

rating_reservations.reason: This task exposed audio clips, MIDI editing, a VST3 instrument, volume, pan, mute, solo, bus/send routing, naming, save, and two export formats. I did not explore effects or more advanced composition features.

The MIDI hint, note Pencil, numerical property keypad, Mixer labels and export menus let me finish using the mouse. Repeating a one-bar melody needed many clicks and playback recovery interrupted the flow.
The dark interface, teal waveforms, clear piano notes and visible routing lines look coherent and attractive. The Mixer has a lot of unused space with only three channels.

Drawing, duplication, numeric edits and mix controls visibly responded quickly. WAV rendering took roughly tens of seconds and playback needed retries; elapsed session time includes tool and screenshot overhead.

Duplicate is a tool that requires clicking a clip after selecting it. Mixer controls moved vertically when a status banner appeared or disappeared, making follow-up clicks uncertain. I also misread a key on the on-screen keyboard and corrected the name.

I found all requested task features: audio, MIDI notes, the installed VST3, volume/pan/mute/solo, bus/send, project save, WAV and MIDI export. Playback was unreliable in this laboratory session, and broader plugins or advanced production features were not tested.

Visible MIDI hint, Pencil drags, Duplicate instructions, mixer labels and the on-screen naming keyboard enabled all requested editing and file operations. Exact trimming and shifting controls needed correction.
The dark interface, turquoise waveform and note clips, and large mixer strips looked coherent and readable.
Most editing actions responded promptly. WAV export visibly took several seconds and playback repeatedly stopped with an output-stream error, interrupting the task. This is not a benchmark.
Most actions had clear labels. Pan drag direction needed adjustment, precise clip-end snapping was fiddly, and the error banner moved mixer controls underneath subsequent intended clicks.
Found audio and MIDI editing, VST assignment, volume, pan, mute, solo, bus, send, mouse-only naming, save and both exports. Reliable playback was not established in this session.

The empty-lane instruction, instrument assignment, duplication and on-screen keyboard made composition possible with only the mouse. Exact trimming needed a second adjustment, and Mixer controls moved vertically when banners or sends appeared.
The dark interface, teal waveform and note clips, and colored routing arrows looked cohesive and made the finished arrangement easy to scan.
Most edits visibly responded promptly. WAV export showed an elapsed-time indicator; playback required a retry and failed again. This is an interaction impression, not a hardware benchmark.

Duplicate first selected a tool rather than immediately copying; its instruction resolved this. Mixer layout shifts made several attempted pan or solo clicks miss. Playback could briefly resume after a control change despite the preceding failure notice.

Audio, MIDI note drawing, a real installed VST3 assignment, bus/send routing, title entry, project save and both exports were discoverable. Reliable playback was not established in this laboratory session.
